title: Checkpoint: Polar Seas
objective: After this level you can describe the ice and life of the Arctic and Southern Oceans.
summary: The Arctic is an ocean ringed by land; Antarctica is land ringed by ocean. So Arctic ice has lasted years while most Antarctic ice melts within one, and each pole's life fits its ice.

cards.headline: The poles are mirror images: an ocean ringed by land, and land ringed by ocean.
cards.body: That single flip shapes their ice, their water and their life. Let's swap between the poles one more time, with everything this chapter taught.

cards.headline: Two polar seas, side by side

items.label: The Arctic
points: A fresh top layer helps sea ice grow
Polar bears hunt ringed seals on the ice

items.label: The Southern Ocean
points: A current flows west to east around Antarctica
Krill feed penguins, whales and fish
Crabeaters strain krill; Weddell seals chew holes

cards.headline: Why the south's ice is younger
cards.body: The Arctic is an ocean surrounded by continents, so its ice is hemmed in, and ice that survives summers, 2 to 4 m thick, has been more common there. Antarctica is a continent surrounded by ocean. Nothing stops its sea ice drifting north until it melts, so most is less than a year old and usually 1 to 2 m thick. Same frozen seawater, very different lives.

cards.headline: Ice from sea, ice from land
cards.body: Put it together. Sea ice freezes from seawater and squeezes out its salt; icebergs are frozen fresh water from glaciers, built from snow. Ice is only about 9% less dense than water, which is why both float and a berg hides most of itself. And under the southern sea ice, young krill spend the winter. The ice isn't just scenery; it's the floor, the roof and the nursery of the polar seas.

cards.headline: Chapter 8 complete
learned: Arctic: ocean ringed by land; Antarctic: land ringed by ocean
Sea ice squeezes out salt; icebergs are fresh
About 90% of an iceberg hides underwater
Krill, whales and seals all live by the ice
Arctic ice is shrinking about 12% per decade

questions.prompt: Polar Seas recap: why is most Antarctic sea ice less than a year old?

options.label: No land stops it drifting north, where it melts
Icebergs smash it apart every spring
options.rationale: Icebergs don't decide the ice's age.

options.label: It only freezes during the southern summer
options.rationale: It grows in winter, like all sea ice.

options.label: Penguins and seals break it up
options.rationale: Animals rest on it; they don't destroy it.

questions.explanation: Around Antarctica no land hems the ice in, so it drifts north until it melts; most is under a year old.

questions.prompt: Polar Seas recap: which polar region is an ocean surrounded by continents?

options.label: Antarctica
options.rationale: Antarctica is a continent surrounded by ocean.

options.label: The Arctic
Both of them
options.rationale: They are opposites: one ocean, one continent.

options.label: Neither of them

questions.explanation: The Arctic is an ocean surrounded by continents; the Antarctic is a continent surrounded by ocean.

questions.prompt: Polar Seas recap, from Level 72: what happens to most of the salt when seawater freezes into sea ice?

options.label: It is locked into the ice for good
options.rationale: Brine drains out; old ice is nearly fresh.

options.label: It turns into fresh water
It is pushed out of the growing ice
It rises into the air as vapor

questions.explanation: Growing sea ice pushes out its salt; what gets trapped as brine drains out over the years.

questions.prompt: Polar Seas recap, from Level 73: why does an iceberg float with only about a tenth showing?

options.label: Ice is only a little less dense than water
The salt inside it weighs it down
Currents pull the bottom of it downward
options.rationale: Density, not currents, sets how it floats.

options.label: It is anchored to the sea floor

questions.explanation: Ice is about 9% less dense than water, only a little lighter, so about 90% of an iceberg floats below the surface.

questions.prompt: Polar Seas recap, from Levels 75 and 79: why could losing winter sea ice matter to the whole Southern Ocean food web?

options.label: Young krill, the main food of many animals, winter under it
Whales need the ice to rest their calves on
Icefish would lose their antifreeze without it
options.rationale: Their antifreeze is in their blood.

options.label: The circumpolar current would stop flowing
options.rationale: The current is driven by wind.

questions.explanation: Winter sea ice is the krill nursery, and krill are the main food for many larger animals, so ice loss could ripple through the food web.
